nodes.body:
Fixes the `NoStdBuild` jobs, which have been red on every branch since the nightly of 2026-10-16 (seen on #1189 and #1190, which touch nothing `no_std`-specific; `main`'s run of 2026-10-13 was still green).

rust-lang/rust#148413 (merged 2026-10-15) mangles the personality symbol like the other std-internal symbols, so the pre-built `core`/`alloc` now reference `__rustc::rust_eh_personality`, and the `#[no_mangle] extern "C" fn rust_eh_personality()` in `no_std/no_std_test/src/main.rs` no longer satisfies the linker:

```
error: linking with `cc` failed: exit status: 1
  = note: Undefined symbols for architecture arm64:
            "__RNvCs6EUDi8WbMwz_7___rustc19rust_eh_personality", referenced from: ...
```

The change declares the function as `#[lang = "eh_personality"]` (with `#![feature(lang_items)]`), which is what rust-lang/rust's own `no_std` binary fixture (`tests/run-make/no-alloc-shim/foo.rs`) moved to in that PR. The compiler then emits the symbol under whatever name it expects, so the harness builds on nightlies before and after the change. The routine is still never called, since every profile sets `panic = "abort"`; the other shims are untouched.

Verified locally on aarch64-apple-darwin: with `nightly-2026-10-16` the harness fails to link without this change and builds with it, for `--profile unix` and `--profile macos`; with `nightly-2026-10-09` it builds either way.

nodes.body:
Fixes #1193.

## Problem

Since 648c6848 ("Remove unnecessary embedded environment from FnPtr"), a closure gets its environment only from its function's entry in the lib, which closures of the main script don't have. A closure kept by the host and called after the script has finished, with `FnPtr::call`, no longer finds the script's `import`s:

```rust
import "m" as m; keep(|| m::who());
```

fails with `ErrorModuleNotFound("m")` when the kept closure is called. It worked in 1.26.1. The bisect and the repro are in the issue.

## Changes

**Commit 1: AST walker.** Put back `FnPtr::env`, set when a closure literal is evaluated (as before 648c6848), and prefer it to the lib's environment when calling. The bare function name as a variable (6f4ed21f) keeps `env: None`, so the fix for a module's closure seeing the caller's functions stays. `FnPtr` is 48 bytes again. Test: `test_module_closure_keeps_imports`.

**Commit 2: Grain.** The first commit left Grain unchanged, and it hit the same error: the compiler pools closure literals as constants and the VM pushed them with `env: None`.

- The VM now gives a loaded `FnPtr` constant an environment built from its global state, as `get_literal_value` does for the walker. It checks only when the program uses function pointers (`Caps::FN_PTR`), so other programs pay one flag test per constant load.
- `constant_caps` refuses a `FnPtr` that already has an environment, so such a constant is not pooled. The compiler leaves it to the walker instead of writing an artifact that loses the environment and fails the same way when read back. (As suggested in the issue discussion.) I could not get an `env: Some` constant into an AST through the public API, since the optimizer rebuilds scope-constant closures as `Fn("anon$…")` calls, so this guard is defensive.
- Tests: a Grain version of the repro (`a_kept_closure_keeps_the_imports_of_its_script`) and a unit test for `constant_caps`.

## Design note

I did not fragment every closure literal into a residual so that the walker sets the environment. That would stop `a.map(|x| ..)` and similar from lowering, and the Grain `AGENTS.md` says to prefer instructions over fragments. Setting the environment in the VM needs no new opcode and no wire-format change.

## Testing

`cargo test --tests` passes with the default features, `internals,grain`, `bin-features,grain,internals`, and `internals,grain` combined with each of `no_closure`, `no_function`, `no_module` and `no_object,no_index`. The library builds without warnings under several `no_*` combinations.
